title: Piece values

D0.outcome: Says the usual point values: pawn 1, knight 3, bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9; the king is never traded.

D1.outcome: Given two pieces, says which is worth more and by how much, and adds up the material on each side.

D2.outcome: Judges a trade, for example a rook for a bishop and a pawn, as winning, equal or losing material without the values shown.

D3.outcome: Gives a position where a piece is worth more or less than its usual points and says why, treating the values as a guide and not a law.

misconceptions: The point values are exact laws, the same in every position.
Counting pieces instead of their values.
conditions: Pawn 1, knight 3, bishop 3, rook 5 and queen 9 are a rule of thumb for comparing trades.
A trade is good when you receive more points than you give.
contrasts: Giving a rook for a bishop and a pawn is 5 for 4 and loses a point although three pieces change hands.
The colour of the pieces does not change their values.
